newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies rally to mixed closes.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies rally to mixed closes.

text.p: CME hog futures rallied into the close as renewed commercial buying ignited fund demand and pork bellies shot up from early limit losses as a flurry of large buy orders met little resistance, traders said.

Hog futures settled 0.450 cent per lb higher to off 0.350 with August up most and July ending up 0.325 at 82.250 cents. Pork bellies finished up 0.125 cent per lb to off 0.900 after early limit losses of 3.000 cents in July and August. July closed up 0.125 at 81.650 cents and August settled off 0.025 at 81.700 cents.
Cash hog calls turned steady to higher for Thursday which prompted late commercial buying in hog futures, traders said.

Renewed commercial buying and fund short covering ran into thin sell orders after the early break and futures ran, up led by August. Cash hogs were not as weak as expected by mid-week and a developing stronger tone for Thursday prompted the short covering, they said.

Rand Financials turned buyer with Rosenthal Collins and Dean Witter also buyers. R.J. O'Brien spread long July/short August early while FIMAT Futures USA did the opposite. Lind-Waldock spread long August/short December and Rosenthal spread long August/short July and October, pit sources said.
